question_text:
121. Study the following statements :
(a) On April 12, Gagarin woke up at 5.00
(b) He wore a blue space suit.
(c) He travelled in space in Vostok.
(1) (a) and (b) are right but (c) is wrong.
(2) (b) and (c) are right but (a) is wrong.
(3) (a) and (c) are right but (b) is wrong.
(4) (a) and (b) are wrong but (c) is right.
option_a: (a) and (b) are right but (c) is wrong.
option_b: (b) and (c) are right but (a) is wrong.
option_c: (a) and (c) are right but (b) is wrong.
option_d: (a) and (b) are wrong but (c) is right.

question_text:
122. Gagarin was a/an :
(1) space traveller
(2) adventure tourist
(3) physicist at Moscow University
(4) paratrooper

123. '... a convenient and inexpensive way ...'
Choose the word nearest in meaning to the underlined one.
(1) contrite
(2) cordial
(3) handy
(4) cracking

124. One benefit of travelling in the express lift to Gagarin was that :
(1) he did not have to pay for it.
(2) it was very thrilling.
(3) he experienced zero gravity.
(4) he could come down in less time.
option_a: he did not have to pay for it.
option_d: he could come down in less time.

question_text:
125. '... looking at the world passing beneath him.'
The underlined word is a/an _________.
(1) article
(2) preposition
(3) adverb
(4) conjunction

126. Study the following statements :
(a) In his private life Gagarin was a poet.
(b) In the experimental darkroom there was no air.
(1) (a) is right and (b) is wrong.
(2) (b) is right and (a) is wrong.
(3) Both (a) and (b) are wrong.
(4) Both (a) and (b) are right.

127. Gagarin was shut up in a dark room :
(1) as punishment
(2) to meditate
(3) as an experiment
(4) to feel like in a space cabin
option_d: to feel like in a space cabin

question_text:
128. '... and he entered the cabin'
The underlined is a/an ________ clause.
(1) Noun
(2) Adjective
(3) Adverb
(4) Coordinate

129. 'I used to eagerly look forward ....'
Choose the word opposite in meaning to the underlined one.
(1) heartily
(2) uneasily
(3) easily
(4) indifferently

130. Which one of the following statements is true ?
(1) The narrator's home town was in a remote area.
(2) Life was comfortable in all respects.
(3) It was known for an annual fair.
(4) People visited his home town for religious reasons also.
option_a: The narrator's home town was in a remote area.
option_b: Life was comfortable in all respects.
option_c: It was known for an annual fair.
option_d: People visited his home town for religious reasons also.

question_text:
131. Study the following statements :
(a) The writer would be very careful while travelling in the cart.
(b) Inspite of the jerks and jolts, the journey was enjoyable.
(1) (a) is right and (b) is wrong.
(2) (b) is right and (a) is wrong.
(3) Both (a) and (b) are right.
(4) Both (a) and (b) are wrong.

132. Study the following statements :
(a) Children were given enough pocket money on the fair day.
(b) Small children would travel with their parents in a separate cart.
(c) Well-to-do villagers liked to oblige the writer's father.
(1) (a) and (b) are right but (c) is wrong.
(2) (b) and (c) are right but (a) is wrong.
(3) (a) and (c) are right but (b) is wrong.
(4) (a) and (b) are wrong but (c) is right.
option_a: (a) and (b) are right but (c) is wrong.
option_b: (b) and (c) are right but (a) is wrong.
option_c: (a) and (c) are right but (b) is wrong.
option_d: (a) and (b) are wrong but (c) is right.

question_text:
133. The devotees thronged the fair.
Choose the option which is nearest in meaning to the underlined word.
(1) attacked
(2) visited
(3) crowded
(4) appreciated

134. Which one of the following statements is not true ?
(1) People visited the fair for divine blessings.
(2) Most of the people visited the fair only for its market.
(3) Prasad distribution was quite chaotic.
(4) Prasad distributed there was very delicious.
option_a: People visited the fair for divine blessings.
option_b: Most of the people visited the fair only for its market.
option_d: Prasad distributed there was very delicious.

question_text:
135. 'Only a mud track led to the village'.
The underlined word is a/an _________.
(1) Noun
(2) Pronoun
(3) Adjective
(4) Adverb

136. Linguistic competence enables learners to __________.
(1) differentiate grammatically correct and incorrect sentences
(2) speak fluently even if not grammatically correct
(3) know how and when to use the language appropriately
(4) use more and more English
option_a: differentiate grammatically correct and incorrect sentences
option_b: speak fluently even if not grammatically correct
option_c: know how and when to use the language appropriately

question_text:
137. At primary level a teacher generally motivates learners for colouring and drawing as it helps in :
(1) engaging learners to maintain silence in the class.
(2) developing fine motor skills.
(3) entertaining learners.
(4) relaxing the teacher from teaching.
option_a: engaging learners to maintain silence in the class.

question_text:
138. Children learn a language most effectively when they have __________.
(1) a proficient language teacher
(2) a good textbook
(3) inhibition
(4) motivation

139. A teacher promotes group discussion and peer interaction in her classroom. She does not bother to correct spelling or pronunciation errors. She is using ____________ approach in her classroom.
(1) Traditional
(2) Eclectic
(3) Structural
(4) Constructivist

140. You as a teacher find that the language used in the lesson is very difficult for your learners. You simplify the language and also make certain changes in the content to suit your learners. What you have done is called __________.
(1) Adopting
(2) Adaptation
(3) Evaluation
(4) Review

141. Today Raju is very happy as he is going to school. He is the first from his family to come to school. None in his family, not even his parents, had ever been enrolled in any school. Raju is thus a __________ learner.
(1) First generation
(2) Second generation
(3) Marginalized
(4) Minority

142. When you go to teach, you find that the textbook begins with rhymes and picture stories and ends with the alphabet. Which approach does this kind of arrangement suggest in language pedagogy.
(1) Bottom up approach
(2) Top down approach
(3) Eclectic approach
(4) Aesthetic approach

143. When language is learnt naturally and without any systematic practice, it is called :
(1) Erudition
(2) Acquisition
(3) Acceptance
(4) Learning

144. One of the important features of ____________ is that the learners solve problems collectively-either in a pair or in a group.
(1) communicative language teaching
(2) behaviourist approach
(3) whole language approach
(4) structural approach

145. While preparing a Lesson Plan on the topic 'Pollution' what will be your first step ?
(1) Prepare introductory questions
(2) Go through the topics many times
(3) Select teaching aids
(4) Frame objectives
option_b: Go through the topics many times

question_text:
146. A teacher asks her learners to write a paragraph on 'water'. Then the learners start discussing what they have been taught in science and social science classes. Then they begin to write a paragraph on water. This is an example of :
(1) Language in use
(2) Language of science
(3) Language across curriculum
(4) Communicative approach

147. You were born and brought up in a village where everybody spoke Hindi and you too began using this language without going to any school. Later when you went to school you studied English, Sanskrit, Hindi and Urdu. Now, you speak English very fluently. Now which is your first language ?
(1) English
(2) Hindi
(3) Urdu
(4) Sanskrit

148. A teacher brings real-life objects like umbrella, raincoat, screwdriver etc to her class. She asks the learners to describe the objects in two to three sentences. The materials that the teacher brings in the class is technically called __________.
(1) Language input
(2) Teaching instruments
(3) Tools
(4) Realia

149. To teach tense in your class you use two pictures of the same person - one picture taken 15 years ago and another just clicked. You initiate a talk in the class about his present and past - his appearance, his habits. Now, you are using :
(1) Prescriptive Grammar
(2) Structural Grammar
(3) Pedagogical Grammar
(4) Rule based Grammar

150. The statements that describe the knowledge, skills, and attitudes that students should acquire by the end of a particular class or course come under __________.
(1) teaching outcomes
(2) learning outcomes
(3) numeracy outcomes
(4) foundational literacy outcomes
